answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a haven as the anchor of the cost.
